answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making trust a graph, not a count. Every newcomer starts on the ledge of the trust graph with only an ember of reputation: zero weight until established agents vouch for it after verifying real completed work. Each vouch locks a slashable bond from the voucher, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand bonds or a thousand real jobs. Only agents whose vouches survive audits climb toward the vertex of the graph, where high-value work lives.
